title: The Docket — spot the flaws (your EU Law WG material)

items.text: A service under Art 56 TFEU must involve a tangible performance that is provided for free, not for remuneration.
items.ground: The model answer explicitly states this definition and applies it to remote medical consultations, showing that such services fall within the scope of Art 56 TFEU.
items.why: The model answer uses this definition to establish that MediLink's remote medical consultations qualify as services under Art 56 TFEU, which is necessary for applying the free movement rules.

items.text: A service within the meaning of Art 56 TFEU involves a non-tangible performance that is normally provided for remuneration and is of a temporary nature.
items.ground: The model answer explicitly states this definition and applies it to remote medical consultations, showing that such services fall within the scope of Art 56 TFEU.
items.why: The model answer uses this definition to establish that MediLink's remote medical consultations qualify as services under Art 56 TFEU, which is necessary for applying the free movement rules.

items.text: Article 52 TFEU only allows restrictions to be justified if they are necessary and proportionate to the objective pursued, not simply because they relate to public interest.
items.ground: The model answer explicitly cites Gebhard and Laval as examples of cases where such justifications were accepted, and applies this principle to the Slovenian law.
items.why: The model answer argues that the Slovenian law's objective of protecting public health constitutes a valid justification under Article 52 TFEU, which is a key principle for assessing the legality of restrictions.

items.text: Restrictions to the freedom to provide services can be justified on the basis of imperative requirements in the public interest under Article 52 TFEU.
items.ground: The model answer explicitly cites Gebhard and Laval as examples of cases where such justifications were accepted, and applies this principle to the Slovenian law.
items.why: The model answer argues that the Slovenian law's objective of protecting public health constitutes a valid justification under Article 52 TFEU, which is a key principle for assessing the legality of restrictions.

items.text: Article 101 TFEU only applies to formal written agreements between undertakings, not to informal cooperation or public statements of support.
items.ground: The functional definition of an undertaking includes any entity engaged in economic activity, and cooperation can take the form of concerted practice without requiring a formal agreement.
items.why: The law recognizes that cooperation in the form of public statements of support can constitute a concerted practice under Article 101 TFEU, even without a written agreement.

items.text: Article 101 TFEU applies to agreements or concerted practices that restrict competition, regardless of whether they are formal written contracts.
